summary: The latent-trap experiment executed and both comparisons scored as predicted (receipt 656e33fb90f24c58a94928eeeeb938aa): the cluster that had only run with the flag disabled carried a staged commit index of 0 and kept its configuration through the first flagged restart (holds, index 1), then staged a commit index of 9 through its own writes while the flag was on (index 2) and lost the configuration on the next flagged restart (violated, witness index 3, zero servers and no leader). That makes the deciding condition the persisted commit index named in the trigger rather than the flag itself, and shows why one restart right after enabling the feature can look harmless. The interpretation records the refinement as executed, replaces the pending note, and adds it as observed counterevidence. The trigger Fact gains the same receipt as an evidence supplement, and I caught and corrected a content mismatch before submitting: my first version of that entry carried the repair Fact's wording under the trigger Fact's id, so the statement, conditions and source list were restored from the stored record with only the executions and the supplement note changed.
